summary: The safety component is the hard verify/gate stage of the loop. Before any ToolCall leaves the reason stage and reaches act, checker::validation::check_tool_call validates the command/URL/path, PathValidator confines targets to the sandbox, PermissionStore decides whether a PermissionGrant waives confirmation, confirm detects DestructiveOperations, dry_run previews effects without executing, scanner finds leaked secrets and vulnerable dependencies, redact strips secrets from anything fed back to the model, process_env sanitizes spawned child environments, yolo offers a deliberate guard-relaxation with forbidden-path backstops, and audit records every decision as an AuditEvent. It can block, redact, preview, or wave through a ToolCall — reshaping loop control at the boundary between deciding and doing.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with safety read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where it sits inline as the last gate before a tool executes and every decision lands in the append-only audit trail.

examples.title: Gate every ToolCall through check_tool_call
examples.intent: Ensure no ToolCall reaches the act stage without passing SafetyChecker validation.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: checker::validation::check_tool_call sits between reason and act; a failed check short-circuits the iteration back to reason instead of executing, and a SafetyBlock is audited.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge from the reasoner node into the safety gate node so every emitted ToolCall is routed through check_tool_call.
touch_interaction.visual: The gate renders as a hexagon with a shield glyph; the inbound edge pulses amber while a check is in flight, green on pass, red on block.

examples.mini_scenario: The reasoner emits a shell ToolCall running rm -rf build; check_tool_call flags it, the gate raises a block, and the loop returns to reason for an alternative.
examples.pitfall: Do not let any tool path bypass the gate; a single un-gated edge defeats the whole verify stage.

examples.title: Confine file targets with PathValidator
examples.intent: Prevent file ToolCalls from escaping the allowed directory set.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PathValidator::validate plus is_path_in_allowed_list run per-path before act; an out-of-sandbox target blocks the transition before any filesystem mutation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the path node to open a radial menu pinning the allowed roots used by is_path_in_allowed_list.
touch_interaction.visual: A dotted boundary ring animates around the node; inside paths pulse blue, escaping paths flash a red slash badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A write ToolCall targets a path outside the workspace; validate rejects it against the allowed list and the write never reaches disk.
examples.pitfall: Build the validator with PathValidator::new from the real working dir; an empty allowed list either blocks everything or nothing, depending on the fallback.

examples.title: Resolve symlinks before validating the target
examples.intent: Follow symlinks and lexical traversal so the real target is what gets checked.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: lexical_normalize_path collapses ../ segments and check_symlink_safety resolves links before act, so a path that looks inside the sandbox cannot launder an outside target.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press a file node to trace its symlink chain rendered as a hop path ending at the resolved target.
touch_interaction.visual: Symlink hops draw as dashed arrows; any hop that leaves the boundary ring flashes red and the parent node blocks.

examples.mini_scenario: A write targets logs/latest which symlinks to /etc; check_symlink_safety resolves the link and blocks the escaping write.
examples.pitfall: Validate the resolved target, not the link path; a link inside the sandbox can still point outside it.

examples.title: Fast-path authorized calls with PermissionStore
examples.intent: Let pre-authorized ToolCalls run without pausing the loop for confirmation.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PermissionStore::is_authorized matches an incoming ToolCall against stored grants; a match skips the human-in-the-loop pause and the control loop stays in continuous execution.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the permissions sub-node to list active grants; each chip shows its tool pattern and resource scope from with_resource.
touch_interaction.visual: Matched grants render as green key badges; the fast-path edge glows steady green while confirmation edges dim.

examples.mini_scenario: A session grant for read_file matches an incoming read ToolCall, so is_authorized returns true and the loop executes without a prompt.
examples.pitfall: Scope grants tightly with with_resource; an over-broad pattern silently waves through unintended ToolCalls.

examples.title: Expire temporary grants on the loop timeline
examples.intent: Auto-revoke permissions after a duration so the fast path narrows over the run.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PermissionGrant::temporary creates a time-boxed grant; once is_expired flips true, is_authorized stops matching and the control loop re-inserts the confirmation pause.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the permission chip to inspect its countdown; the chip shrinks as time-to-expiry drains.
touch_interaction.visual: Temporary grants carry a draining ring timer; on expiry they gray out and drop from the active set.

examples.mini_scenario: A temporary run_shell grant expires mid-session; the next shell ToolCall no longer matches and the loop re-prompts the operator.
examples.pitfall: Re-check is_authorized on every ToolCall; grants expire between iterations, so caching an authorization decision leaks stale trust.

examples.title: Decompose compound shell commands before gating
examples.intent: Validate every segment of a chained shell command independently.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: split_shell_commands breaks a compound command on &&, ;, and |, and check_shell_command gates each segment; one unsafe segment blocks the whole ToolCall.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap a shell node to expand its segments into a chain of mini gate chips, one per sub-command.
touch_interaction.visual: Each segment chip lights green or red; a single red chip turns the parent node red and halts the edge to act.

examples.mini_scenario: git pull && rm -rf build is split; the first segment passes but the second is flagged, so the whole call is blocked.
examples.pitfall: Check every segment; a benign prefix must not launder a dangerous suffix through the gate.

examples.title: Catch tee and redirect writes hiding in shell commands
examples.intent: Surface file writes smuggled through shell redirection or tee, not just the write tool.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: shell_tee_write_targets and shell_output_redirect_targets extract implicit write paths from the command string and feed them back through PathValidator before act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread on a shell node to fan out the extracted write targets as small file chips beside the command.
touch_interaction.visual: Each extracted target renders as a file chip; out-of-sandbox targets glow red and veto the parent command.

examples.mini_scenario: echo data | tee ../../outside.conf looks like a read-only pipeline, but shell_tee_write_targets extracts the path and the sandbox check blocks it.
examples.pitfall: Never gate only the command name; redirection and tee turn a 'safe' command into an arbitrary file write.

examples.title: Pin DNS to block SSRF and rebinding
examples.intent: Prevent tool HTTP calls from reaching private or internal addresses.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PinnedDnsResolver resolves the host once and is_private_or_internal rejects private ranges before the act stage opens a socket, closing the check-then-connect rebind window.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the network guard to toggle localhost and private-range allowances.
touch_interaction.visual: The guard renders a globe inside a firewall ring; a resolution to a private IP flashes a red block badge on the edge.

examples.mini_scenario: A fetch ToolCall resolves its host to 169.254.169.254; is_private_or_internal returns true and the gate blocks the cloud-metadata request.
examples.pitfall: Connect to the pinned IP from PinnedDnsResolver, not a fresh lookup; re-resolving between check and connect invites DNS rebinding.

examples.title: Classify each tool's RiskLevel for routing
examples.intent: Attach a risk tier to every ToolCall so the loop knows how loudly to gate it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: classify_tool_metadata maps a tool name to ToolMetadata with a RiskLevel; the control loop uses that tier to decide between silent pass, confirm, and block.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a tool node to reveal its ToolMetadata card: RiskLevel badge, category, and read-only flag.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes tint by risk — green low, amber medium, red high — with higher tiers pulsing faster.

examples.mini_scenario: A network fetch is classified medium risk; the loop routes it to the confirmation branch instead of running it silently.
examples.pitfall: Keep default_tool_metadata current; an unclassified tool falls back to a default tier that may over-prompt or under-guard.

examples.title: Return an explicit PermissionResult per call
examples.intent: Make the allow/deny/confirm outcome an inspectable object, not a bare boolean.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PermissionChecker::check returns a PermissionResult that the control loop branches on; normal_mode_needs_confirmation decides whether the current ExecutionMode pauses for a human.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a pending ToolCall to reveal its PermissionResult card with the decision and matched grant.
touch_interaction.visual: Allowed cards glow green, denied red, needs-confirm amber with a waiting-spinner badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A medium-risk ToolCall under normal mode gets a needs-confirmation PermissionResult; the loop pauses and the operator approves it.
examples.pitfall: Branch on the PermissionResult, not on the risk tier alone; ExecutionMode changes what the same tier means.

examples.title: Detect destructive operations before they execute
examples.intent: Recognize destructive shell and git operations and force a confirmation gate.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: detect_destructive_shell_command and detect_destructive_git_operation classify a ToolCall into a DestructiveOperation with a RiskLevel; requires_confirmation then holds the act transition until ConfirmResult arrives.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a flagged node to see the DestructiveOperation description and its color-coded RiskLevel.
touch_interaction.visual: Flagged nodes show a hazard stripe; the confirm edge pulses amber until a ConfirmResult lands, then snaps green or red.

examples.mini_scenario: A git push --force ToolCall is caught by detect_destructive_git_operation; the loop pauses, the operator confirms, and the push proceeds.
examples.pitfall: requires_confirmation must key off the detected operation, not the tool name — a plain-looking shell command can still be destructive.

examples.title: Preview high-risk acts with dry-run
examples.intent: Show what a ToolCall would do without executing it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: preview_tool_call builds a DryRunPreview and display_preview renders it; the loop verifies intent on the preview and only then commits the real act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the gate to toggle dry-run; queued acts render as ghost previews via display_preview instead of running.
touch_interaction.visual: Dry-run nodes render translucent with a dashed 'DRY' badge; no side-effect glow fires on their edges.

examples.mini_scenario: A batch of file edits is previewed with display_batch_preview; the operator reviews the diffs and approves, releasing the real writes.
examples.pitfall: The preview must come from preview_tool_call's own simulation; a hand-written 'what I would do' string drifts from what the tool actually does.

examples.title: Scan payloads for secrets and dangerous patterns
examples.intent: Block or flag ToolCalls whose content leaks credentials or carries dangerous code.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: scanner::scan_content runs the loaded patterns over args and output, producing findings that the gate uses to block, redact, or annotate before act or feedback.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the scanner sub-node to expand the finding list with location, snippet, and severity.
touch_interaction.visual: Findings stack as severity-colored bars; the node pulses while a scan_content pass is active.

examples.mini_scenario: A commit ToolCall's diff contains an API key; scan_content emits a critical finding and the gate blocks the push.
examples.pitfall: Scan both inbound args and outbound results; secrets leak just as easily through tool output fed back to the model.

examples.title: Weight findings by severity score at the gate
examples.intent: Decide block-versus-warn from aggregated severity, not raw finding count.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: scanner's score, risk_score, has_critical, and has_high aggregate findings into a threshold decision that branches the verify stage between block, warn, and pass.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread to fan out findings sorted by score; drag a threshold slider to set the block cutoff.
touch_interaction.visual: Findings arrange on a heat gradient; everything above the slider glows red as a blocker, the rest stay amber warnings.

examples.mini_scenario: Two low findings and one critical arrive; has_critical forces the block branch even though the count is small.
examples.pitfall: Blocking on raw count invites noise; weight by severity score so many low findings never outweigh one critical.

examples.title: Audit dependencies before an install act
examples.intent: Flag ToolCalls that add or use known-vulnerable dependencies.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: audit_dependency checks a dependency against recorded advisories and is_vulnerable produces a finding the verify stage surfaces before a build or install act proceeds.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the dependency node to list packages with a vulnerability badge, fixed version, and advisory URL.
touch_interaction.visual: Vulnerable deps render with a red bug badge and CWE tag from with_cwe; clean deps stay muted.

examples.mini_scenario: An add-dependency ToolCall pins a version flagged by is_vulnerable; the gate warns and shows with_fixed_version before the install runs.
examples.pitfall: Match on name and version together; a fixed patch release of the same package must not inherit the older advisory.

examples.title: Redact secrets before output re-enters context
examples.intent: Strip credentials from tool output, JSON, and paths before they reach logs or the model.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: redact_secrets rewrites tool result content, redact_json cleans structured payloads, redact_path masks home-dir prefixes, and safe_log wraps printing — keeping the feedback edge into reason clean.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge from the tool-output port through the redact node before it loops back to the reasoner.
touch_interaction.visual: Redacted spans render as black bars in the output preview; the node carries a masking-tape icon.

examples.mini_scenario: A log-reading ToolCall surfaces a bearer token; redact_secrets replaces it before the output is appended to the conversation.
examples.pitfall: Redact before output is appended to messages or checkpoints, not after; once persisted, the secret is already exposed.

examples.title: Sanitize the environment at process spawn
examples.intent: Strip sensitive variables from the environment handed to spawned child processes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: process_env::sanitize_command_env filters the env at the moment the act stage spawns a child, preventing credential inheritance across the loop boundary.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the shell node to inspect which env vars sanitize_command_env will strip for the next spawn.
touch_interaction.visual: Denied vars render as struck-through chips on the node; a filter-funnel badge marks the scrub point.

examples.mini_scenario: A shell ToolCall would inherit a cloud API key; sanitize_command_env strips it so the child process cannot read the credential.
examples.pitfall: Scrub at spawn time for each ToolCall; caching a scrubbed env leaks variables added later in the session.

examples.title: Log every execution and block as an AuditEvent
examples.intent: Persist a durable JSONL trail of tool executions and safety blocks for replay and forensics.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AuditLogger::log_tool_execution and log_safety_block append an AuditEvent on every gated decision, giving the loop an observable history without altering control flow.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick up on the audit node to scroll the append-only event stream in a side panel.
touch_interaction.visual: A ticking log ribbon streams entries; execution rows are grey, safety-block rows carry a red tag.

examples.mini_scenario: log_safety_block records a blocked destructive command; the AuditEvent lands in the session JSONL for later review.
examples.pitfall: Never mutate past AuditEvents; the log is append-only and its integrity is the basis for post-hoc trust.

examples.title: Bracket the run with session audit markers
examples.intent: Emit session-start and session-end events that bound the run's audit trail.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: log_session_start and log_session_end frame the whole loop lifecycle, giving replay tooling clean boundaries for each run.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick down on the audit node to jump to the session-start marker; flick up for session-end.
touch_interaction.visual: Start and end markers render as bold bookend bars anchoring the event ribbon.

examples.mini_scenario: The agent boots and log_session_start writes an opening AuditEvent; on shutdown log_session_end closes the trail for that run.
examples.pitfall: Emit the end marker even on failure paths, or partial audit trails complicate forensic replay.

examples.title: Relax guards deliberately with YoloManager backstops
examples.intent: Let an operator run fully autonomous while hard backstops and auditing stay on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: YoloManager::should_auto_approve collapses the confirmation pause for the run, but is_forbidden and is_protected_path still block the worst targets, record_operation keeps count, and audit_summary closes the books.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotate the mode dial on the gate node from Guarded to YOLO; a warning overlay requires a confirming tap before it commits.
touch_interaction.visual: The gate turns high-contrast orange with a lightning badge; protected-path backstops stay lit red to show they remain armed.

examples.mini_scenario: An operator enables yolo for a sandboxed batch job; ToolCalls auto-approve, but an rm on a protected path is still refused by is_protected_path.
examples.pitfall: Yolo removes confirmation, not auditing or the forbidden-path backstops; never let it also disable the sandbox or the log.
